narrative.overview:
Kinlight looks the way a well-run building tells you where to go. Warm charcoal enamel sign panels sit inset on a cool light ground, hairline rows carry the information, and square-capped drawn arrows point to where each thing went. The result reads as technical and professional, and stays warm: every neutral leans toward brown, and the single accent is amber. The site's core picture is one post, signposted to everywhere it went.

The density is that of good signage: few elements, large type, and each row saying one thing. The base size is 18px, or 22px with the A+ control, because buyers skew older and read between tours on a phone, iPad or office desktop. The system is light only, set in daytime materials, and depth comes from the contrast between panel and ground, with shadow kept to a few objects that sit on top.

This system refuses saturated yellow, the user's standing direction for the look. It also refuses the white split-hero software page and the dark neon page.
keyCharacteristics: Warm charcoal sign panels inset from the page edge, on a cool light ground.
Hairline rows, not cards, as the default way to list things.
One amber accent, for the primary action and for what is live or current.
Overpass for everything that signposts, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for everything that is read.
Large type by default, with a persistent larger-text control.

rules.name: The Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: Amber does two jobs: it marks the way forward (the primary action, route and jump arrows) and it marks what is live or current (status words, live tags, the current page, the booked time). A list arrow that only marks an item stays neutral, and a tag that is not live stays neutral.

rules.name: The Three Ambers Rule
rules.body: Pick the amber by its ground. Fills use Amber Signal with Navy on Amber text (5.3:1), charcoal uses Bright Amber (7.2:1), and light grounds use Deep Amber (5.3:1 on stone, 4.7:1 on deep stone). Amber Signal as text on stone is only 2.75:1, and Deep Amber on charcoal is only 2.3:1.

rules.name: The Selected Is Ink Rule
rules.body: A chosen option in a group inverts to Logo Navy with Soft White text: text size, form intent, language, tour date. Amber waits until the choice is confirmed, as with the booked time in the tour sample.

rules.name: The Sign Face Rule
rules.body: If it points, names or labels, it is Overpass: headings, nav, buttons, tags, row titles. If it is read as a sentence, it is Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, and form labels and message text stay there too.

rules.name: The Schedule Numeral Rule
rules.body: Overpass Mono is for schedule numerals in sample screens and nothing else: it sets the times in a site calendar and the dates in a tour picker. It never sets prose, headings or labels. Prices stay in Overpass with tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Everything Scales Rule
rules.body: Sizes are in rem, on a root of 112.5% (18px) that the A+ control raises to 137.5% (22px). A pixel font size would ignore the reader's choice.

rules.name: The Next Door Rule
rules.body: Pages form a sequence, and each ends with a full-width next-page row that names where it goes, followed by the closing panel: Home, How it works, Why Kinlight, Pricing, Questions, then Founding pilot. Founding pilot ends the sequence, so its form stands alone with no next-page row or closing panel.

rules.name: The Flat Sign Rule
rules.body: Signs are mounted flat, so panels never take a shadow. Lift belongs to tools and sample screens sitting on a light ground.

rules.name: The Square Cap Rule
rules.body: Arrows and chevrons are drawn strokes with square caps, heavy for their size (5 units on a 48-unit box). They come in three directions, each with a meaning: up-right, right and down. They are not icon-font glyphs or rounded icon-set arrows.

dos: Do keep the look technical and professional but warm: charcoal and stone that lean brown, with amber as the only accent.
Do choose amber by its ground: Amber Signal for fills, Bright Amber on charcoal, Deep Amber on light.
Do list things as hairline rows before reaching for cards.
Do keep every font size in rem, so the A+ control scales the whole page.
Do keep buttons and toggles at 2.75rem or taller, with a visible 3px focus ring on every ground.
Do caption every sample screen as a sample, using the fictional Wren Hollow.
Do state errors in words as well as color.
Do end each page in the sequence with a next-page row.
donts: Don't use saturated yellow in any fill, accent or field.
Don't build the white split-hero software page or the dark neon page.
Don't spend amber on decoration: a list arrow, a tag that is not live or a heading stays neutral.
Don't use Amber Signal as text on stone, or Deep Amber as text on charcoal.
Don't put a shadow on a sign panel.
Don't set prose, headings or labels in Overpass Mono.
Don't add eyebrows above headings or section numbers.
Don't make any content depend on an animation to be visible.
